controller_naming: The DCS graphs have no controller tag and no block types. Controller names are the PDF's loop names (P1-PC, P1-LC, P1-FC, P1-TC, P1-CC). Measurement/output names are the DCS graph node names.

sheet_1001_PCV01_PCV02.question: sheet 1001 drives PCV01 and PCV02 from one block: split range or two loops?
sheet_1001_PCV01_PCV02.answer: One loop, one PID, two valves. Not two loops. Whether it is split range is not stated.
docs_say: PDF p.8 (text + Fig. 4): P1-PC is one feedback loop for two pressure-control valves (PCV01D, PCV02D) holding PIT01 at setpoint B2016. The figure shows a single PID, saturation and rate limiter; the output goes to PCV01D directly and to PCV02D through a function block F(.).

PDF p.9-10 (text + Fig. 9): the same loop drawn as Ovation blocks; block 1001.21 emits DM-PCV01-D, which goes to 1001.22 (PCV01) and to 1001.23, which emits DM-PCV02-D to 1001.24 (PCV02). dcs_1001h.json has the same links.
PDF p.43 (case study, attack scenario AE05): manipulating DM-PCV01-D in 1001.21 also affects PCV01 and PCV02 data, i.e. PCV02 is derived from the PCV01 command.
PDF p.26 attack table: P1-PC lists only P1_PCV01D as its CV.
sheet_1001_PCV01_PCV02.docs_do_not_say: The words split range do not appear; the characteristic of F(.) (split range, ratio, offset, sequencing) is not given, nor its ranges.
sheet_1001_PCV01_PCV02.how_listed: P1-PC/PIT01/PCV01 in loops.csv and P1-PC/PIT01/PCV02 in loops_leg2.csv, following this repo's one-list-per-leg convention (bayer_loop_lists in scripts/corpus_matrix.py). This is a list-format choice, not a claim that the valves are split ranged.

sheet_1003_TIT01_into_FT01_FT02.question: sheet 1003 joins TIT01 into the FT01/FT02 paths: cascade?
sheet_1003_TIT01_into_FT01_FT02.answer: The PDF says P1-TC is a cascade (temperature outer loop, flow inner loop) with feed-forward on water flow. It does not name the inner flow controller, and it does not say whether FT02 is the inner loop's measurement or only the feed-forward input. FT01 is not part of the loop. Left unresolved; not in loops.csv.
docs_say: PDF p.8 text: P1-TC is a feedback loop for two flow-control valves (FCV01D, FCV02D) holding TIT01 at setpoint B4022, using cascade control with feed-forward compensation to the flow controller (inner loop).

PDF p.9 Fig. 7: outer PID (B4022, TIT01) then saturation and rate limiter into a summing junction; FT02 through a function and rate limiter also enters that junction; the sum drives a second PID whose output goes to FCV01D directly and to FCV02D through a function F(.). The second PID has no separate measurement input drawn.
PDF p.27 attack table: P1-TC CV1 P1_FCV01D, PV1 P1_TIT01 (AP19/AP20). PDF p.27 AP22 and PDF p.29 AP45 give the P1-TC setpoint as P1_B4002, not B4022 as in Fig. 7.

PDF p.13 tag list: B4002 heat-exchanger outlet temperature setpoint; B4005 temperature PID control output; B400B water outflow rate setpoint (heating water tank, l/h); B4022 temperature demand for thermal power output control.
sheet_1003_TIT01_into_FT01_FT02.docs_do_not_say: No tag for the inner (flow) controller; whether FT02 is the inner PV or a feed-forward; which of B4002/B4022 is the outer setpoint (the document gives both); that B400B is the inner setpoint (only suggested by its description and unit).
sheet_1003_TIT01_into_FT01_FT02.graph_observation_not_documentation: In dcs_1003h.json FT01 reaches only the HMI (1003.19 -> 1003.20 -> 1003.21 -> HMI PV), so FT01 is display-only on this sheet. FT02 has two paths: 1003.4 -> 1003.5 -> 1003.26 (joins the TIT01 path from 1003.25) and 1003.6 -> 1003.8 (DM-FT02Z) -> 1003.11, which also takes HMI setpoint block 1003.10. The sheet has two HMI setpoints (1003.10, 1003.18) merging at 1003.30 before DM-FCV01-D; Fig. 7 shows one setpoint. The graph alone cannot say which block is a PID, a summer or a selector.
sheet_1003_TIT01_into_FT01_FT02.what_a_person_must_decide: Either (a) one I/O-level row P1-TC,TIT01,FCV01 (+ FCV02 leg) as the attack table treats it, or (b) cascade rows: outer P1-TC,TIT01,<inner controller tag>, inner <tag>,FT02,FCV01 (+ FCV02 leg), which needs a name for the inner controller and confirmation that FT02 is its PV.

drawing_side.summary: phy_boiler.json is a process (energy-flow) graph, not a P&ID. It has 41 equipment/sensor/valve nodes and 67 links, but no controller nodes and no signal lines, so a key.json built from it would have no controller symbol and no signal_edges, and every loop would come back not drawn. Signal edges could only be made by merging it with the DCS graphs through the DM- point names, and the loop list itself comes from the DCS sheets and PDF, so that audit would be circular.
drawing_side.what_it_does_give: Node ids usable as printed text (PIT01, PCV01, PCV02, LIT01, LCV01, FT03, FCV03, TIT01, FT02, FCV01, FCV02, TWIT03, PP04 ...), a desc per node, and in_tags/out_tags naming the DCS points (e.g. PIT01 out DM-PIT01; PCV01 in DM-PCV01-D out DM-PCV01-Z). That supports at most a tags-present check, and a process-topology check (corpus row 8, pipe topology).
drawing_side.link_codes: Each link has dynamics 1, 2 or 3 (45, 14 and 8 links). The PDF never states the numbers, but PDF p.47 Fig. 19 labels every edge Hydro&Thermo, Hydro or Thermo, and matching edges one by one gives 1 = Hydro&Thermo (equipment-to-equipment flow, grey), 2 = Hydro (to level/level-switch/pressure/flow sensors, blue), 3 = Thermo (to temperature sensors, heater -> TK02, HEX tube <-> shell, red). Checked examples: TK01->TWIT03 = 3 (red Thermo in Fig. 19), PCV01->PIT01 = 2 (blue Hydro), HT01->TK02 = 3, TK01->PP04 = 1. So the codes can be confirmed from the PDF figure by correspondence, not from a written legend.
drawing_side.defects_seen: The node attributes type, device and dynamics are the same 41-entry tuple copied onto every node and are not aligned with node order (e.g. TIT01 would read Valve, PCV01 Pressure), so per-node types must not be read from them; use desc and the id prefix instead. FCV01's in_tags is P1_FCV01-D where every other node uses DM- names. PP01 in the DCS sheets is PP01A/PP01B here.
